meta.title: Use of Stop Watch in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To accurately measure and record time intervals during pharmacognosy experiments including extraction, maceration, percolation, and distillation procedures.
sections.scope: Applicable to all timed operations in the Pharmacognosy laboratory including extraction procedures, sedimentation tests, and stability assessments.
procedure: Verify battery level before use — replace if display is dim or shows low battery warning.
Press the 'Reset' button to set the display to 00:00:00 before starting any timing procedure.
At the precise moment the timed event begins (e.g., addition of solvent, start of heating), press 'Start'.
Allow the stopwatch to run without disturbance during the timed procedure.
Press 'Stop' at the exact end of the timed event.
Read the elapsed time from the display immediately and note it in the laboratory record.
For lap timing (e.g., recording multiple time points in an extraction), use the 'Lap' button to record intermediate times without stopping the main timer.
After all readings are recorded, press 'Reset' to clear the display for the next use.
If the stopwatch is battery-operated, check battery voltage at the beginning of each practical session.
For critical timing experiments, use two stopwatches in parallel as a cross-check.
Store the stopwatch in a clean, dry location away from corrosive chemical vapours.
precautions: Calibrate the stopwatch against a reference time signal (e.g., IST broadcast) periodically.
Do not expose the stopwatch to water, acids, or organic solvents.
Replace batteries as soon as low-battery warning appears — never use with a failing battery for critical measurements.
For very precise timing (< 1 second accuracy required), use a calibrated digital timer instead.
Do not drop or subject the stopwatch to mechanical shock.
Record the stopwatch ID in the experiment record if multiple stopwatches are in use.
